method: Asked what document is for: durable explainability under privacy minimisation, not cache policy.

Blind re-derivation of 'what answers why' for three finding shapes from architecture/04 fact plane: (1) local lint/pattern, (2) path/relationship (cycle, blast radius), (3) negative/absence (dead code).
Compared each shape to T0/T1/T2 retained sets WITHOUT assuming lint-shaped SARIF regions.
Cross-checked product thesis that graph/blast-radius is the wedge (04) against T1 default justification in 06/V10.
Did not use author's 'cited span is what users need to act' as a premise — re-tested it.
whatCouldHaveFailed: T1 sufficient for all finding classes → accept default
T1 only wrong for rare rules → accept-with-carveout
T0 already retains enough facts for relationship/negative why → reject thin-T1 concern

authorDoubt.question: Does T1 answer why for relationship findings (cycles, blast radius, dead code) that may have no citable span the way a lint finding does?
authorDoubt.authorPosition: T1 default because spans answer why; T0 cannot; T2 is a source archive.

findingShapes.whyRequires: primary subject span + optional local AST context
findingShapes.T0: identifies what fired; not source text

findingShapes.whyRequires: an ordered proof path (or SCC member set) of edges with enough endpoint identity to re-trace; optionally a span per hop for display
findingShapes.T1PrimarySpans: INSUFFICIENT if 'spans cited' means primary locations only — showing three package roots does not explain the cycle circuit
findingShapes.T0: SUFFICIENT only if retained 'facts' include the edge set (or a sealed path certificate) used in the proof, not merely digests of fact chunks

findingShapes.whyRequires: closed-world claim: Coverage of the reference relation over declared scope + the subject identity; there is often no positive reference span to cite
findingShapes.T1PrimarySpans: Shows WHAT is dead; does not prove WHY (exhaustive absence). Excerpt of the dead symbol is display, not proof.
findingShapes.T0: Answers why only if Coverage certificates and relation roots remain; that is structural, not excerpt

independentAnalysis.ambiguityInT0: The T0 row lists 'facts' without saying whether full fact bodies for the Run's required relations are pinned or only content digests. If digests only, T0 cannot re-answer path or absence either. If full facts, relationship why lives in T0 and T1's unique value is source text for human display — which is not the same as proof.
independentAnalysis.productFit: architecture/04 states call graphs, dead-code, blast radius, package cycles are the same query engine and that agent workflow / blast-radius trust are the wedge. A default explainability tier sized for lint spans is therefore misaligned with the product's own center of gravity.

findings.title: T1-as-cited-spans is lint-shaped; quietly too thin for relationship and negative findings
findings.detail: V10 insight 'you need the spans it cited' is true for local predicates and false as a general theory of explainability. Cycles and blast-radius membership are explained by paths/edge sets; dead code is explained by Coverage-complete absence. If T1 retains only primary source excerpts, the default cannot answer why for the wedge capabilities. That is not a residual edge case — it is the default being wrong for the product thesis.
findings.requiredFix: Redefine T1 as a sealed finding-local evidence payload: for each finding, the proof object the rule emitted (path certificates, SCC member lists, negative-query Coverage digests + relation roots) PLUS optional display excerpts. Do not equate 'excerpt' with 'why'.

findings.title: Default tier cannot be justified until T1's retained set is proof-complete for all shipped rule classes
findings.detail: RT residual correctly says the default carries almost all the weight because loosening is impossible. Shipping T1=excerpts as default freezes a lint-shaped floor. Options: (a) redefine T1 as above and keep it default; (b) keep excerpt-T1 but set default to a higher tier for path/negative rules; (c) require rules to declare minExplainTier and refuse seal below it. (a) is preferred — one default, proof-complete.
findings.requiredFix: Either expand T1 retention definition before seal, or make default rule-class-relative with loud disclosure. Do not seal ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS with excerpt-T1 as universal default.

findings.title: T0 'facts' is under-specified; underdetermination collapses the ladder
findings.detail: If T0 pins full required-relation fact bodies, path/absence why is largely T0 and T1 is mostly UX. If T0 pins only hashes/digests, neither T0 nor excerpt-T1 answers relationship why — only T2 or a missing T1.5. The ladder needs an explicit statement of what 'facts' means at T0.
findings.requiredFix: Specify T0 fact retention: which relations, whether bodies or digests, and whether proof objects are first-class evidence pins separate from snapshot blobs.

findings.title: Privacy accounting for path proofs may exceed 'small' T1
findings.detail: A blast-radius path can cite many files; an SCC can be large. Expanding T1 to proof objects reintroduces source-adjacent data (identifiers, paths, possibly snippets per hop). Size and privacy class must be bounded (link to v1-F3/v2 bandwidth finding) or T1 becomes a stealth T2 for graph rules.
findings.requiredFix: Bound path-certificate cardinality; privacy-class path proofs; inventory must show T1 cost for graph-heavy Runs.

findings.title: Amendment authority vs design correctness correctly split in register; prose could still be read as settled
findings.detail: 06 marks the section candidate inline — good (method rule 8). The star-default table still presents T1 as product-default with high confidence language. Readers may treat presentation strength as seal.
findings.requiredFix: Mark the default row itself as candidate hypothesis pending A1-RT-01 resolution.

verdictOnAuthorDoubt.answer: No — excerpt-T1 does not answer why for relationship or negative findings.
verdictOnAuthorDoubt.therefore: T1 as currently defined is quietly too thin; the default is wrong until T1 means proof payload, not only spans.

sealRecommendation: Do not seal ARCH.RETENTION-TIERS. The amendment direction (tiered, declared, honest degradation) is right; the T1 definition and default are not yet merited.
whatWouldChangeMyMind: A T1 schema showing path certificates and negative Coverage objects as required fields for those finding kinds, with golden explainability tests.
Or product decision that graph relationship rules are non-goals for durable explainability (contradicts 04 wedge — would need 04 amended too).
positiveObservations: Recognising the V1 vs absolute-explainability contradiction was necessary and correctly framed as amendment not mitigation.
RT-1..RT-5 (manifest field, one-way degradation, forward-only config, inventory, fail-loud T2 requirement) are sound independent of the T1 content bug.
T2 read-set-bounded not repo-bounded is correct.
knownLimitations: Did not implement a proof-object schema; only stated requirements.
Did not measure byte sizes of real cycle/blast findings from the existing product (steering may not constrain design; sizes would be illustrative only).
